definition: Primary narrative footage, typically the speaker or principal action; the label describes editorial role, not a file type.
example: Interview explanation stays audible under the cutaway.

definition: A historical display boundary used to avoid placing essential action too near an edge; modern platforms have their own overlays.
example: Check delivery-specific phone interface overlays.

definition: The panel currently receiving keyboard commands, which changes the meaning of some keys.
example: J/K/L may operate the Source Monitor or timeline depending on focus.

definition: Encoder data rate controlled by a target and sometimes a maximum, rather than a constant amount per frame.
example: Test VBR target and maximum on a motion-heavy passage.

definition: An extra channel storing transparency, often 0 transparent to 1 opaque.
example: A lower third with transparent background needs an alpha-capable format.

definition: Signal strength, commonly shown as a waveform; audio meters usually display level on a logarithmic dB scale.
example: Clip peaks are higher in some spoken syllables than others.

definition: Unwanted visible or audible distortion introduced by source capture, processing or compression.
example: Banding in a gradient or blockiness in fast motion.

definition: Displayed width divided by height.
When image shape differs from its intended display or sequence, causing stretch, letterbox, pillarbox or crop.
example: A 4:3 archive shot needs intentional framing in a 16:9 sequence.

definition: Preparation of decoded or resampled audio for reliable timeline use; it may generate temporary media-cache data.
example: A compressed audio clip can need conforming before waveform playback.

definition: A compressed picture that can be predicted from other frames; not every codec uses the same prediction structure.
example: Long-GOP footage may require extra decode work during random scrubbing.

definition: Supporting picture over the primary story.
example: Show the product while narration explains its mechanism.

definition: Number of signal levels per channel before processing/encoding.
example: 8-bit has 256 code values per channel; 10-bit has 1024.

definition: Data per second of encoded stream.
example: 8 Mb/s for 10 s is about 10 MB before overhead.

definition: Text rendered permanently into the exported video pixels.
example: Captions remain visible in a player even without external subtitles.

definition: The captured original file or card structure to retain independently of proxies or transcodes.
example: Keep camera media untouched before creating editing proxies.

definition: Constant bitrate aims for predictable stream size.
example: A broadcaster may specify CBR.

definition: Assignment of source audio channels to timeline channels; incorrect mapping can mute or duplicate a microphone.
example: Assign a recorded mono lav channel appropriately before a dialogue cut.

definition: Reduced color resolution relative to brightness.
example: 4:2:0 sacrifices chroma detail versus 4:2:2.

definition: Wavelength-dependent color fringing, sometimes a lens defect and sometimes a stylized effect.
example: Inspect red/cyan fringes around high-contrast edges before sharpening.

definition: A placement of referenced media in a sequence.
example: Same camera file used twice at different in/out ranges.

definition: Compression group that can be decoded without referencing pictures from a different group; useful for some interchange workflows.
example: Seek and transcode behavior differs between GOP settings.

definition: Compression/decompression method for a stream.
example: H.264 or ProRes is not a folder or container.

definition: Range of reproducible colors in a defined color space.
example: Wide-gamut camera footage must be mapped appropriately for Rec.709 delivery.

definition: Tags describing how image values should be interpreted by a decoder or display pipeline.
example: Wrong primaries or transfer tags may make an exported file appear different in a player.

definition: Collecting or copying relevant files for project handoff, often with optional trimming depending on tool and media type.
example: Reopen the archived project from a disconnected drive to test links.

definition: A file whose presentation timestamps follow a regular target cadence, unlike VFR footage.
example: Transcode a drifting phone recording to an editing-friendly CFR intermediate.

definition: File wrapper that houses encoded streams and metadata.
example: MP4 may contain H.264 video and AAC audio.

definition: Overlapping audio levels that smooth transitions.
example: Two room-tone clips crossfade over 8 frames.

definition: Decibels relative to digital full scale.
example: 0 dBFS is the upper digital sample peak limit.

definition: Process of reconstructing color channels from a camera sensor mosaic, relevant to some RAW media.
example: RAW decode quality and controls depend on camera format and support.

definition: Read compressed source frames into pictures or sound samples available for editing.
example: A CPU may struggle to decode 4K 10-bit long-GOP footage during scrubbing.

definition: Convert interlaced fields into progressive pictures, with possible motion or detail tradeoffs.
example: Inspect old broadcast material for combing before export.

definition: Small controlled noise that can reduce visible quantization artifacts when changing precision.
example: Very smooth gradients can show banding in low-bit-depth delivery.

definition: Labeling adjustment at 29.97-related cadence; actual video frames are not discarded.
example: Some timecode frame numbers are skipped to align clock labels.

definition: Adobe inter-application linking between timelines/compositions.
example: Linked After Effects composition appears in Premiere.

definition: Difference between the darkest useful detail and brightest recoverable values of a signal.
example: Log camera footage needs a suitable transform before creative grading.

definition: A collection of output settings; it is a starting point, not proof that delivery requirements are met.
example: Verify actual resolution, profile, color and audio against client specifications.

definition: Whether even or odd scan lines are presented first in an interlaced signal.
example: Wrong field order can cause jerky motion in older formats.

definition: Frames displayed per second (nominal or exact).
example: 25 fps frames have 40 ms intervals.

definition: Nonlinear relationship between code values and light/display intensity.
example: Incorrect gamma interpretation changes midtone appearance.

definition: Transforming colors from one gamut to another while managing out-of-range values.
example: Map wide-gamut footage to the chosen SDR output without arbitrary clipping.

definition: Group of Pictures; compression referencing frames over time.
example: Long-GOP camera codec can be hard to scrub.

definition: High dynamic range encoding and display path.
example: PQ/HLG footage needs managed transforms for SDR exports.

definition: Level margin before clipping or target maximum.
example: Dialogue peaks below 0 dBFS leave room for transient summation.

definition: High Efficiency Video Coding / H.265.
example: Usually more efficient compression than H.264 but variable decode support.

definition: First chosen frame in a marked range.
example: Source In at frame 50 and Out near 100 selects a portion.

definition: Compression that predicts frames from other frames.
example: Long-GOP codecs use interframe prediction.

definition: Compression primarily operating within each frame rather than using temporal prediction across frames.
example: An edit-friendly intermediate may scrub more smoothly than a long-GOP camera codec.

definition: Compression of each frame substantially independently.
example: ProRes is commonly chosen for edit intermediates.

definition: Incoming audio begins before its matching video.
example: Hear the next speaker before seeing them.

definition: Time/value control point for animated property.
example: Scale goes 100% to 110% in 2 seconds.

definition: Method used to calculate values between keyframes, such as linear versus eased motion.
example: Ease a lower third into position without an abrupt stop.

definition: Outgoing audio continues under the next picture.
example: Keep interviewer speaking beneath illustrative B-roll.

definition: Horizontal bars created when a wider image is fitted inside a narrower display or frame.
example: Choose intentional letterboxing instead of stretching cinema footage.

definition: Camera encoding that preserves wide scene range with low contrast preview.
example: Normalize camera Log before creative grading.

definition: Perceptual program loudness measurement.
example: Integrated LUFS describes the complete segment.

definition: Approximate perceived brightness component, distinct from a simple average of RGB values.
example: Use waveform scopes to compare scene exposure.

definition: Lookup table mapping input to output values.
example: Technical Log transform and creative LUT serve distinct roles.

definition: High-quality intended deliverable or source reference.
example: Retain source camera masters and edit-friendly output master.

definition: Project has a reference to source media, but it cannot currently resolve the file location.
example: Relink a moved folder while checking clip identity.

definition: Descriptors about footage and edits.
example: Timecode, duration, reel, frame rate and tags.

definition: One channel of audio signal.
example: Lavalier dialogue is often mono.

definition: An algorithm predicting movement between images.
example: Optical Flow may warp a fast-moving hand.

definition: Multiple synchronized cameras in one editorial source.
example: Cut between two synced interview angles.

definition: Audio carrying more than two discrete channels; routing depends on track and export mapping.
example: Confirm the intended channel layout before a broadcast master.

definition: Placing a sequence inside another sequence as one editable timeline item.
example: Nest a built title montage for higher-level placement.

definition: Editing through references rather than irreversible linear recording.
example: Move a clip anywhere without cutting the camera file.

definition: Boundary defining the end of a chosen source/sequence range.
example: Mark after the sentence, then insert only the selection.

definition: Transcript-based selection and rough-sequence creation in 26.5.
example: Select two statements to generate a new sequence.

definition: Maximum instantaneous signal amplitude.
example: A loud clap peaks higher than sustained dialogue.

definition: Vertical sidebars when narrower footage is shown in a wider frame without stretching.
example: A portrait clip may need reframing rather than black sidebars.

definition: Shape of individual sample pixels.
example: Modern HD often uses square pixels; legacy media may not.

definition: Position of current playback/edit time.
example: Move playhead to 00:00:10:00 before adding marker.

definition: Material or time before the main recorded action, used for handles or sync.
example: Retain a few seconds before the slate/clap in original footage.

definition: Editable set of media pointers, bins and sequences.
example: A .prproj alone does not contain camera originals.

definition: Temporary media rendered to improve playback.
example: Green render bar does not prove final export quality.

definition: Alternate lower-cost file attached to master.
example: Edit 4K originals with 720p proxies.

definition: Link from the original media object to a lightweight edit copy; original media remains authoritative for normal final export.
example: Toggle proxies, then inspect final output at original resolution.

definition: Mapping values onto discrete code levels; insufficient precision can produce banding or audio noise.
example: Gradient artifacts become more obvious after aggressive compression.

definition: SDR video color primaries/transfer conventions.
example: Common SDR broadcast/web delivery target.

definition: Temporary computed media for smoother playback; using previews in exports requires attention to preview quality and settings.
example: A green timeline render bar does not prove the final H.264 export settings.

definition: Boundary trim moving later sequence content.
example: Shorten A by 10 frames; B begins 10 frames earlier.

definition: Boundary trim that transfers duration across adjacent clips.
example: Grow A 10 frames and shrink B 10 frames; no length change.

definition: Guides for keeping critical text and imagery away from cropped edges or platform overlays.
example: Preview captions on the final vertical-phone layout.

definition: Image values describing captured scene light before a display rendering transform, depending on the color system.
example: Preserve Log/HDR interpretation before applying a creative look.

definition: Timeline and settings defining an edit.
example: 1080p25 sequence stores tracks and timebase.

definition: Frame-rate ruler used by the editing timeline; distinct from source frame rate and export frame rate.
example: A 25 fps sequence counts output positions in 25 frames per second.

definition: Exposure-time representation affecting motion blur; a 180-degree shutter nominally means half-frame exposure.
example: Different motion blur makes two cameras harder to match.

definition: Move a clip in sequence by trimming neighbors.
example: Shift middle insert without changing its own source range.

definition: Shift source content while keeping clip sequence interval fixed.
example: Use earlier part of reaction shot without moving the cut.

definition: Panel for examining source media and marking a usable source range before an edit.
example: Set source In and Out points before Insert.

definition: Choose destination tracks for inserted source audio/video.
example: Patch V source to V2 before inserting an overlay.

definition: Track rule about participation in ripple edits.
example: Lock allows protected alignment decisions.

definition: Frame-address display in hours:minutes:seconds:frames.
example: 00:01:10:12 is a position, not 70.12 seconds.

definition: Frame address advancing from the last frame number of a second to the next second.
A use of source media with its own timing/effects/position; it is not a rewritten camera file.
example: Two cuts from one video can have different color corrections.

definition: Sequence-track designation for many timeline operations.
example: Track-target highlight differs from source V1 patch.

definition: Mapping between numeric image values and represented brightness, such as SDR gamma or HDR PQ/HLG.
example: Matching primaries alone does not ensure correct HDR-to-SDR display.

definition: Estimated peaks between reconstructed digital samples.
example: Output limiter may target true-peak ceiling.

definition: Nonconstant video capture frame intervals.
example: Phone footage may require CFR transcoding for sync.

definition: Variable bitrate reallocates data with picture complexity.
example: Action may use more bits than a static slate.

definition: Variable frame rate: video frames arrive at varying time intervals; some sources need conversion for dependable sync.
example: Phone footage that drifts against separate recorder audio.

definition: Relative channel correction for neutral reference.
example: Correct warm orange camera cast before look.

definition: Internal processing representation for tone/color.
example: May differ from source and output color space.

definition: Structured data for supported editorial exchange.
example: Not every effect/transcript transfers between editors.

definition: Video representations separating luma-like and chroma-like components; YCbCr is the digital family commonly used by encoded video.
example: 4:2:0 sampling stores less chroma spatial detail than 4:4:4.
